data.claim:
A shared company AI toolkit (clone: commitments, principles with stable ids, stack guides, 16 skills, guides, ADRs, templates, installer/builder/validator, prose lint) vs ddflow. P=PRESENT PA=PARTIAL A=ABSENT.
MAPPING element -> ddflow today -> gap ids.
1 Tiered promises above rules, only a recorded time-boxed exception waives: PA. Rule enforcement strengths + pinned rules + r-* rules + gates enforce; company floors tighten-only (D-GP-Q4/Q5, DEP-lifecycle); exception = expiring waiver via approvals engine. No commitments tier name, waiver not built. GP-waiver, RQM-strength, SEC-policy, LP-override-record, LP-kinds-coverage (deviations and waivers as layered kinds).
2 Rules with stable permanent ids, retire-by-deprecate not renumber: P. ddflow rule add --id, rule edit/remove (tombstone), rule search/show. No id-prefix registry, no citation check.
3 Deviation allowed, silent deviation not (cite id and reason): PA. GP-waiver has a deviation counter for best-practice; no record kind linking a diff or item to a rule id plus reason. Gap: nothing parses a cited id in a completion note or commit and checks it exists. Candidate: deviation kind (LP-kinds-coverage names it).
4 Precedence 0..4: PA. Config layers default<company<project<local<user (D-config-layer-order, D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06) govern CONFIG; promises are not a layer. Reconcile: a commitment is a rule whose waiver needs a recorded expiring exception AND whose check is a gate, so even the highest layer (user) cannot tick it off without the exception record; enforced company floor (D-config-layer-order tail) is the mechanism. Task prompt below commitments = agent session cannot waive (person-only commands).
5 File-scoped stack guides emitted per IDE (applyTo): PA. rule --globs scope is injected on claim; per-harness native emission from one source is GC-agent-files (open, needs GC-decide, ADP-managed-files); inventory of what each harness loads is B-rules-inventory (running); import of others' files B-rules-import (needs B-path-rules-to-decisions). Detected-by-dependency selection: B-onboard detection exists for stacks of the project, not for per-stack rule packs.
6 Skills as slash commands and .agents/skills, bundle for chats without files: PA. ddflow prompts list|show|get|eject (MCP prompts/get), docs templates P-doc-templates; skills dir emission and an agent-neutral bundle are GC-agent-files. No skill catalogue for lifecycle skills (SPEC-docs, GC-spec-stage, PO-*, TM-* open, per earlier talk research).
7 Task card (skill, effort, model by kind; raise/lower effort rules): PA. task --kind exists; GV-complexity-score (open) derives tier/effort; adjustment rules as data not built; the earlier proposed task-card decision (D-task-card-fields once filed) covers fields. Gap: effort-delta rules as a layered table keyed by risk signals, and enforcing the card at claim.
8 One task per fresh chat: PA. Claim leases an isolated worktree per item, one lane per task; session context mark knobs; no refusal when an agent drifts to a second item (WP-plan-notice, CC-resume-pack open).
9 Installer (idempotent, dry-run, never overwrite project-owned files, update = pull and rerun): P/PA. ddflow adopt/onboard, upgrade, ManagedFile ownership marker (adapters/managed_files.py), DRV-packs digest-pinned company packs, D-CM-Q9. Missing: a company BASELINE importer from a repo clone at runtime (see decision D-company-baseline-importer-2026-11-11).
10 Generated references never hand-edited plus --check in CI: PA. ddflow docs check (extracted surface vs docs), pins regenerate, generated-region sha; no per-skill reference generation. The pattern to take: a generated-file marker + digest check applied to every emitted agent file (GC-agent-files).
11 Structural validator (name==dir, description<=1024, body<=200 lines, task-card vs metadata agree, no tool placeholders, links within skill): ABSENT for skills/rule packs. ddflow has lint for descriptors (model lint) and docs check. Idea: pack lint as a gate for imported/company packs.
12 Prose gate (deterministic linter run in CI, filler/hedge/narration words): PA. SC-gate-binding (open) binds a tool to a gate; [gate.*] command gates already run any command with exit code as evidence, so a prose linter is configurable TODAY as a command gate, absent as a shipped companion.
13 ADR status Draft/Active/Retired + ADR for structural change: P. decisions proposed/accepted/superseded, decision applicable by globs; doc lifecycle states exist in doc types. No Retired(archive) separate from superseded: acceptable.
14 Model analysis log (candidate vs baseline on same inputs, rubric, runs): PA. DRV-model-catalog (facts as data), SW-ledger (first-pass gate rate per family/model/kind), reviewer ledger; GV-eval, tests/eval only tool_diet. A continuous comparison log record kind is absent.
15 Governance escalation log (issue, routed to, status): PA. approvals engine, session ask, research/lesson records; no escalation record with routed-to and resolution reference (nearest: SEC-findings, P-change-mgmt). The toolkit's own log is an empty table: weak.
16 CODEOWNERS, PR template, CI workflow: PA. flow.integration=pr, pr_reviewers, pr status/sync/threads; BL-pr-evidence-template, BL-branch-policy-check open (from the workflow-diagram research).
17 Change-type evidence table (rule change needs rationale+exception considered+real example+two owners; skill change needs before/after eval on two providers): PA. ddflow has cross-family reviewer rule, rule add --check dedupe; skill eval on realistic prompts across providers is absent (earlier talk research idea 11).
18 Token-cost table of what loads each request: PA. B-rules-inventory reports always-loaded bytes/tokens per agent; MCP lean profile, charter caps; a doctor report listing per-request load by layer is the missing view (CC-cache-policy).
19 Effort/model by phase (spec on capable model, slices on fast): PA. GV-*, D-model-routing, TE-limit-aware-routing; no phase->model table bound to the workflow profile (WP-profile-bind).
20 Changelog entry per user-visible change as a checked item, release-notes skill that refuses to invent: PA. ddflow version cut/show, export changelog from log; gate for 'changelog line present' absent; cheap to add as command gate.
21 Spec readiness audit (coverage verified independently, closed models, open questions=0, verdict READY/GAPS/NOT READY): PA. WP-task-ready (definition of ready), WP-rows-document, US-ready; the audit as a readiness gate with the verdict contract is not built. Strong idea.
CAN DDFLOW RUN THIS WORKFLOW BY CONFIGURATION: PARTLY. Works now: pipeline of stages as phase tasks with needs; kind_pipelines; per-kind gate lists; command gates for validators and a prose linter; rule scope globs; human approvals; worktree per task; ddflow prompts for skill-like commands; company layer via DRV-packs. Missing: (a) baseline importer that reads a clone, (b) agent-file/skill/instruction emission (GC-agent-files), (c) effort-delta rules and task card, (d) deviation and exception records, (e) readiness gate, (f) workflow profile binding stages to gates (WP-profile-bind).
RECIPE today: phase 'delivery' with tasks discover->spec->audit->slice->implement->review->notes each needs the previous; kinds research/spec/code/docs; gates.kind_pipelines maps spec kind to [research, rules, critic] and code kind to the normal pipeline; a [gate.prose] command gate runs the linter over docs globs; approvals gate on the spec task; rule add --pin for the three promises; rule add --globs per stack; model/effort recorded in the task body until GV-* lands.
IDEAS RANKED value/effort:
1 deviation record plus citation check (high/low-med): kind under LP-kinds-coverage; completion note must cite rule ids it deviated from; layered, default off.
2 commitments tier = rules marked non-waivable except by an expiring approved exception (high/med): enforcement value plus GP-waiver; company floor; project cannot lower.
3 readiness-audit gate with a verdict contract (high/med): WP-task-ready plus a gate type 'audit' with coverage ratio and open-question count.
4 company baseline importer (high/med): read a clone path, map to rules/prompts/doc types/pack, digest-pinned, zero copying into the repo, shown as origin company layer.
5 effort-delta rules as data (med/low): table of signals->delta in config, evaluated at claim, advisory first; extends GV-complexity-score.
6 per-harness emission of file-scoped instructions from one source (high/med): GC-agent-files; note the native formats differ (applyTo in Copilot, globs in Cursor, paths in Claude rules).
7 pack lint (structural validator) for imported skills/rules (med/low): size caps, name==dir, description cap, no tool-specific placeholders; a gate on import.
8 prose gate companion (med/low): bind a linter via SC-gate-binding; ship nothing, document a recipe.
9 load-per-request doctor report (med/low): extends B-rules-inventory with per-layer tokens; budget knob with warning.
10 model-comparison log kind with rubric and cadence trigger on model release (low-med/med): SW-ledger is data source; SJ-* scheduler is trigger.
Also: an install plan preview (check whether ddflow adopt and onboard print a plan before writing), installed-version report across projects (MR-views), changelog-line gate, escalation record, Draft/Active/Retired mapping.
WHERE DDFLOW IS AHEAD: enforced gates with unavailable-is-not-pass; event log provenance and replay; layered config with person-only override; cross-family reviewers; bug needs failing test; approvals engine; worktree leases for parallel agents; cost/price facts as data; stable layered rules with enforcement strength rather than prose-only guidance. TOOLKIT WEAKNESSES: guidance is advisory and requested not enforced; the task card is manual model picking in an IDE picker; assumes one IDE; the validator checks only the toolkit's own layout, so consumers get no validation except prose lint; copies of skills and instructions are overwritten on update so local changes are lost and staleness is possible; size/token budget is stated but measured only by hand (400-1100 tokens per skill); governance, model-analysis and training folders are empty tables (placeholders); no evidence of effort-rule backtest, rules cite ids only by convention; ADO skills embed organisation-specific names and custom fields, so they are not portable; commitments DI and SD are still proposed, only one adopted.
EARLIER TALK RESEARCH: this toolkit CONFIRMS the task-card, layers and runs-per-merge ideas (same card and effort rules in data form, install flow, precedence), REFINES them (effort adjustments are a small signal table; commitments tier; deviation citation; install writes files per IDE) and shows no contradiction. It also shows the talk's 'seven parts' as real folders and that the vale-only prose gate is in fact the only consumer-side validator.
AZURE DEVOPS (from the two ADO skills, read in full). DATA MODEL: demand ticket (other project) -> Epic -> 5 standard architecture Tasks (diagram update, technical design doc, architecture doc, kickoff meeting, create features) + Features (title by outcome never layer; layer split goes into child User Stories). Epic fields: title, type, area and iteration path, state New, assignee, priority 2, value area, a custom demand-number field, custom application and project fields, description, related link to the demand; Tasks: Activity=Design, original/remaining/completed work hours, parent link; Features: description and acceptance criteria from a design doc section, priority, value area, inherit iteration/assignee/demand, parent link to the Epic. WORKFLOW: read demand -> duplicate check by WIQL on demand field (skip Rejected) -> ask before write -> create Epic -> link related to demand -> create Tasks with parent links -> companion docs prefilled from templates with TODO markers, never invented -> separate explicit request: parse design doc, propose features, confirm, create, link, report table. TOOLS: az CLI with azure-devops extension (az boards work-item create/show/relation add, az boards query --wiql), PAT in AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT or az login; REST PATCH for rich-text fields. No MCP.
COMPARISON: demand=ddflow proposal/requirement; Epic = phase (or a phase group), Feature = phase or task group, Task = task, Story = task. ddflow has no tracker kind; external sync today observes sibling-repo items only; forge port is pull requests/checks/issues/releases for GitHub/GitLab/Gitea; IA-forge (open) names Azure DevOps for PR state; CP-intake (open) tracker sync and idempotent create over a feed with fields as data and trust=imported; PO-feedback-import and TM-defect-forge (open) use ForgePort with consent and receipts. B173 abandoned and folded into IA-forge. Import (ddflow import) reads files only (todo, adr, journal), dry-run by default, ids read not invented, idempotent, max_tasks guard.
ADO ADAPTER DESIGN. 1 Port WorkItemPort (not ForgePort: work items are not PRs) in ddflow/adapters, Protocol + registry + fake + conformance test (r-adapters): get(id), query(wiql or filter), children(id), create(type, fields, parent), update(id, patch), link(id, rel, target), comments. 2 Adapter az-cli (shell out via the command runner, no token held; unavailable when az or login missing) first; REST over the HttpClient port second (PAT from the secrets port, never printed, Basic auth, api-version pinned). 3 Consent: every contact is outward (r-consent-outward): consent recorded once per organization/project and kind; read-only consent does not cover write. 4 Read-only first: `ddflow import --from workitems <epic-id>` dry run lists Epic->phase, Feature->phase (or task group) , Task/Story->task, hierarchy links ->phase membership, related/predecessor links -> needs, acceptance criteria -> task acceptance text; imported text fenced trust=imported; source id kept in a source ref (idempotent key = org/project/id plus rev). 5 Mapping is DATA (type map, field map, state map) in a company layer file, so no custom field name lives in code (the toolkit's custom demand field stays in the user's config). 6 Write-back second, behind approval T2+: status changes, link to merged PR, comment with receipt; create (epic-creator, feature-creator equivalents) as a recorded PLAN first, executed after person approval, with duplicate check by query on the mapped demand field and receipts keyed by plan item for idempotence. 7 Conflict: ADO revision number stored; if remote rev moved, refuse write and show a three-way diff; ddflow wins only on fields it owns (state, PR links), ADO owns title/description/priority/assignee/area/iteration. 8 Outside ddflow: area/iteration paths, estimates in hours, board columns, assignments, capacity, test plans. 9 Auth: az login, PAT env var via secrets port, managed identity; scope to Work Items read/write only. 10 Limits: WIQL result cap 20000, batch get 200 ids per call, rate limited by TSTUs with retry-after: paging and backoff in the adapter with deadlines (r-bounded-everything). 11 Tests: fake WorkItemPort with scripted trees and revisions; recorded fixtures for az JSON; conformance run against both; no network in this repo; a live smoke test is operator-run, opt-in. 12 MCP: no new top-level tool: `ddflow import` and `ddflow update` families take a source argument; surface budget stays.
CONFIDENTIALITY AND LICENCE: no licence file or copyright header in the clone; an internal package lookup and ADO skills carry internal organisation URLs and custom field names; template for an architecture doc carries a third-party attribution (CC BY 4.0). Therefore nothing is copied; the importer treats the clone as a user-supplied source and shows its origin.
data.falsifier: A ddflow knob or task already delivers an element marked ABSENT or PARTIAL (a deviation kind, a readiness-audit gate, per-harness instruction emission, a work-item port), or a recipe step in the worked example is refused by ddflow when tried on a sample project.
data.mechanism: Read the whole toolkit clone as data (README, guides, commitments, principles, stacks, 16 skills with assets, ADRs, templates, knowledge, installer/builder/validator source, CI, prose-lint styles), nothing executed; mapped each element to ddflow commands, config keys and open task ids via ddflow help, rule/gate/companions/docs/prompts help and ddflow show of the covering tasks.
data.probe: ddflow help; ddflow rule add --help; ddflow import (help topic); ddflow docs --help; ddflow companions --help; ddflow prompts --help; ddflow gate --help; ddflow flow --help; ddflow show IA-forge CP-intake GP-waiver LP-kinds-coverage SC-gate-binding GC-agent-files B-rules-import B-rules-inventory GV-complexity-score ADP-forge PO-feedback-import TM-defect-forge
data.probe_output: No work-item or tracker kind exists; IA-forge lists Azure DevOps among forges for PR state and is open; ADP-forge (done) has ForgePort for GitHub, GitLab, Gitea; CP-intake open; GP-waiver, LP-kinds-coverage (names deviations and waivers), GC-agent-files, SC-gate-binding, B-rules-import open; B-rules-inventory running; ddflow import reads files only.
data.question: Can ddflow adopt the patterns of a shared company AI toolkit (rules with stable ids, skills, task card, installer, prose gate, ADRs) and its Azure DevOps epic and feature skills by configuration plus a runtime importer, and what should be taken?

api-version 7.1); https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/boards/work-items/guidance/agile-process (Epic>Feature>Story>Task); https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/boards/work-item; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/integrate/concepts/rate-limits. data.alternatives: Copy the content into ddflow defaults (rejected: confidentiality, licence, staleness). Ask each project to run the toolkit installer (rejected: writes files outside ddflow ownership, no layering, no gate).
data.consequences: Needs a mapping spec per source format (data, in the company layer), a read-only dry run, and a drift report when the clone moves. Harder: format changes upstream break mapping, shown as unavailable. Costs one importer, no second loader (LP-kinds-coverage, B-org-kinds).
data.context: Operator answer 2026-11-11: patterns only, import at runtime; confidentiality and licence of the clone unknown (r-consent-outward). D-config-layer-order and D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06 already define the stack; DRV-packs gave digest-pinned company packs.
data.decision: ddflow may offer an importer/adapter that reads a company AI-toolkit clone the user points at (path or url, pinned by commit or digest), maps its rules, instruction files, skills and templates onto ddflow kinds, and presents them as the company baseline layer (default < company defaults < company policy < project < local < user). Nothing from the clone is copied into the repository or shipped defaults; the layer records origin, commit and digest; a person consents once per clone; a pack lint refuses oversized or malformed items as unavailable, never passed.
data.title: A company baseline importer reads a user-pointed clone at runtime and copies nothing into the project

data.alternatives: Free-text in the completion note (rejected: not queryable). Waiver only (rejected: too heavy for best-practice).
data.consequences: Adds one kind, a citation parser and a layered default of off. Risk: noise; mitigated by strength filter.
data.context: A shared toolkit states 'deviate allowed, silent deviation not'. ddflow has deviation counter language in GP-waiver but no kind or citation check.
data.decision: Introduce a deviation kind (under LP-kinds-coverage and GP-waiver) linking an item or change to a rule id and a reason. For best-practice strength rules a deviation is recorded by the agent; for required rules it needs an expiring waiver through the approvals engine. Completion notes and reviewers may cite rule ids; a check refuses a cited id that does not exist. Silent deviation is detected, not assumed.
data.title: A deviation is a record kind: rule id, reason, scope, and who approved, cited at completion

data.alternatives: Treat as pinned block rules only (rejected: no waiver discipline). Leave to company policy only (rejected: projects need local promises).
data.consequences: Needs enforcement strength 'commitment' (tighten-only), exception record with expiry (LP-override-record, GP-waiver) and a review at expiry. Harder: another tier to explain.
data.context: A toolkit precedence puts promises above prompts; ddflow D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06 puts the user highest for config.
data.decision: Name the highest rule tier commitments: few, always loaded in one line, outrank task instructions and every config layer including user; the only way past one is a recorded exception with scope, risk, mitigation, expiry and a named approver via the approvals engine (person only). Layer order still governs config; commitments are enforced as company floors plus gates, so user-highest and non-waivable do not conflict.
data.title: A commitments tier is rules marked non-waivable except by an expiring approved exception, enforced by gates not by layer order

data.alternatives: Extend ForgePort (rejected: work items are not pull requests). Only a prompt calling az (rejected: no consent, receipts or idempotence).
data.consequences: Overlaps CP-intake and IA-forge: sequence them or fold the port under CP-intake. Needs fixtures of az JSON and a fake; live smoke is operator-run and opt-in.
data.context: Operator asked for an Azure DevOps adapter for epic and feature creation from demand and design documents. IA-forge (open) covers only PR state for Azure DevOps; CP-intake (open) covers intake and sync generally.
data.decision: Add a WorkItemPort in ddflow/adapters (Protocol, registry, fake, conformance test) separate from ForgePort. First adapter drives the az CLI (no token held), second uses the HTTP adapter with a secrets-port token. Read-only import maps Epic and Feature to phases, Task and Story to tasks, hierarchy to membership, dependency links to needs, acceptance text to the task, source id plus revision as the idempotent key; type, field and state maps are data in a layer. Write-back (state, PR link, comment) and plan-then-create of epics and features need recorded consent and approval; remote wins on title, description, priority, assignee, paths; ddflow owns state and links. No new top-level MCP tool.
data.title: External work items (Azure DevOps first) go through a WorkItemPort, read-only import before any write-back, mapping as data
